title: Analog Read Serial
description: Wire a 10k potentiometer to an analog input pin and print its changing value to the Serial Monitor as you turn the knob.

steps.clip: Let's gather what we need: an Arduino Uno, a half breadboard, a 10k potentiometer, and a few jumper wires.
Pick up the potentiometer and push all three of its legs straight down into the breadboard, each in its own column.
hints: The three legs should land in three neighboring columns, straddling no gap.
The middle leg is the wiper — that's the one we'll read from later.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one outer leg of the potentiometer to a GND pin on the Arduino.
hints: Either outer leg can be the ground side — swapping it just reverses which way the reading changes as you turn the knob.
Black is the usual wire color for ground.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the other outer leg of the potentiometer to the 5V pin on the Arduino.
hints: This supplies power so the potentiometer can produce a range of voltages.
Red is the usual wire color for 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the middle leg of the potentiometer, the wiper, to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: A0 is one of the analog input pins, labeled A0 through A5.
This wire carries the voltage that changes as you turn the knob.

steps.clip: Upload the code, then open the Serial Monitor and turn the knob to watch the numbers change between 0 and 1023.
